verdict.strongest_supported_claim: The activation transaction at 2025-05-13T11:27:06Z mechanically created a positive creator-vault balance delta (+10,732 lamports), establishing that the creator-fee rule bundle was economically live and mechanically incident on creators. Beyond that, the evidence supports only descriptive findings: post-activation Pump gross and 7-day quality cohorts show large, statistically significant declines in launches, unique creators, graduated_7d counts, and the 7-day graduation rate relative to pre-period levels and relative to the rejected Moonshot comparison. These are before/after contrasts at a platform-wide event date with no accepted control, so they are consistent with — but do not identify — an effect of the fee bundle. No welfare claim for traders or the platform is supported at all.
verdict.summary: One identified mechanical incidence fact (creator vault delta); all behavioral/thickness outcomes are descriptive; welfare incidence for every stakeholder is unidentified.

fatal_issues: no_valid_control: Moonshot is the only other platform and fails the control gate on two independent grounds — concurrent product changes (confounded treatment contrast) and potential displacement/interference of Pump users (SUTVA violation). The comparative_hac7 estimates are therefore not difference-in-differences treatment effects; they are descriptive cross-platform contrasts.

treatment_bundle_not_separable: The intervention simultaneously changes creator subsidy, trader fee burden, and a program upgrade. Even a valid before/after contrast could not attribute any effect to the fee mechanism versus the upgrade; the estimand is at best a reduced-form bundle effect, as the machine output itself states.

internal_contradiction_in_7d_sample: The quality_7d_21d launches outcome shows a statistically significant negative pretrend (estimate -0.014, p = 0.000126), which invalidates the parallel-trends-type assumption for that specification. The largest and most-cited negative estimates come from a sample whose own pretrend test fails.

internal_contradiction_in_30d_sample: quality_30d_21d shows significant nonzero pretrends for launches (p = 3.7e-16) and graduation_rate_30d (p = 2.7e-05), again undermining the before/after comparisons in that sample; the corresponding post estimates are mostly insignificant anyway.

timing_and_anticipation_mechanics: Although the anticipation window (May 8–13) is excluded, the seven-day quality cohorts ending 2025-04-30 protect only the pre side; post cohorts in quality samples are constructed from post-activation launches whose 7-day outcomes extend past the sample end and may be partially observed or selected on survival/migration, which is itself a treatment-correlated outcome.

graduation_rate_composition: The comparative graduation_rate_7d estimate (-0.0146, p = 0.0014) contrasts with the Pump-only before/after estimate (~0.0001, p = 0.79). The significant figure depends entirely on the rejected control; within-Pump there is no detectable rate change, only fewer launches. Apparent 'quality decline' is likely a level/composition artifact, not a rate effect.

welfare_unidentified_by_construction: H3 correctly reports that trader net welfare requires counterfactual execution costs, behavioral response, and liquidity/quality response — none observed — and platform welfare requires net revenue, retention, and market-share response — none observed. A positive mechanical transfer to creators is not a welfare result; incidence of a fee on traders could exceed the creator transfer.

short_window_and_power: 21 days pre/post with HAC-7 on daily aggregates is a short, heavily autocorrelated series; inference is fragile to the event-date shock structure, and the null 30d quality results may reflect power rather than absence of effect, so they cannot be used as confirming evidence either.

permissible: A creator-vault balance increased by 10,732 lamports in the activation transaction at 2025-05-13T11:27:06Z; the creator-fee rule was economically activated on that date.
A May 12 program-support transaction produced zero creator-vault delta, so support preceded and was distinct from economic activation.

After activation, Pump gross and 7-day quality cohorts show large descriptive declines in launches, unique creators, and graduated_7d counts versus their own pre-period and versus Moonshot (a control that fails the gate).
Within-Pump before/after shows no detectable change in the 7-day graduation rate; the significant comparative rate decline rests on the rejected Moonshot contrast.
prohibited: Any claim that the fee bundle caused the decline in launches, creators, or graduations.
Any claim about market thickness as a causal outcome (thickness effects are descriptive associations only).
Any welfare statement for traders, creators (net), or the platform, including 'creators benefited' — the vault delta is a gross mechanical transfer, not net welfare.
Any decomposition attributing effects to the creator subsidy versus trader fee versus program upgrade.
Any use of the comparative_hac7 coefficients as causal effect sizes.

audit.useful_next_check: Run in-time placebo activations within the pre-period (e.g., pseudo-events on each day of 2025-04-17 to 2025-05-07 using the same pump_before_after_hac7 specification) and report the distribution of placebo estimates relative to the actual -0.187 launches estimate. This is the strongest falsification available without new data or models: it tests whether the observed post/pre drop is unusually large relative to normal pre-period volatility and directly addresses the main surviving alternative explanation (ordinary time-series fluctuation coinciding with the event date). If the actual estimate sits well inside the placebo distribution — which the significant quality_7d pretrend already suggests is plausible — even the descriptive 'unusual break at activation' claim weakens; if it sits in the extreme tail, the descriptive break claim is strengthened while remaining non-causal.
